value: Search for WIMP dark matter via nuclear recoils in cryogenic Ge and Si detectors
Reject electron-recoil backgrounds using simultaneous ionization and phonon (heat) measurement

summary.plain: CDMS II searched for dark matter particles using very cold germanium and silicon crystals half a mile underground in Minnesota. It ran from about 2005 to 2009 and found no convincing signal, but set some of the tightest limits of its time on how often dark matter might bump into ordinary atoms.
summary.technical: Second-generation Cryogenic Dark Matter Search: 19 Ge (~230 g) and 11 Si (~100 g) ionization-and-phonon detectors in five towers, operated below 50 mK at the Soudan Underground Laboratory. The final blind analysis (612 kg-day raw exposure, results submitted Dec 2009) observed two candidate events consistent with background, setting a 90% CL spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section limit of 7.0 × 10⁻⁴⁴ cm² at 70 GeV/c² (3.8 × 10⁻⁴⁴ cm² combined with earlier CDMS II data).

unique_capabilities.quote: Particle interactions in the detectors deposit energy in the form of phonons and ionization.
value: Simultaneous phonon and ionization readout on each detector for event-by-event background discrimination
